title: Apply the smaller halo exponents inside one cell, with normalizer 6 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/gaussian-cell-exponents`. Inside one cell, once the relative weight error is at most `1/(16p^2)` and the ideal off-sums are at most `1-1/(8p^2)`, both 2-norms of the rounded block meet the ceiling used by #4406. The exponents 12, 26, 28, 28 and 7 all apply. The normalizer 7 is not smallest: the inverse ceiling is `16p^2-1`, so 6 already puts it strictly below one.

**Claim type:** conditional exponent arithmetic for that block. **No new κ.** Across-cell entries are not included.

## Lemma

Both rounded gaps are at least `1/(16p^2-1)`. Hence `||A^{-1}||_2 ≤ 16p^2-1` and `||A||_2 < 2`. The polynomial `P = p^{-12} sum_{j<p^{26}} Q^j A^*` then has error `< p^6 exp(-p^2)` and bandwidth `< p^{28}` when the integer bandwidth is at most `p-1`.

| Exponent | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| 12, 26, 28 | sufficient, and still smallest |
| 7, the normalizer | sufficient, but 6 is smallest |
| 5, as a normalizer or error multiplier | fails at `p=2` (`63>32`) |

## Not covered

- The global reference. Across-cell entries are not the gauge ratio.
- Any new κ. The selected record remains `23/10000`.

## Evidence

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-cell-exponents
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/gaussian-cell-exponents outcome=completed
```

Head: `26af8afbadd7f8feb737d98b47ac9f4b45d35c7a`. Base: canonical main `2a13eb1827784206202db90e5dc8327cf8a250db`, priority revision 7.
